prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1240; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound in the right lane of a residential road in Katy, Texas, when the vehicle ahead slowed and Driver 1 applied the brakes. The vehicle struck the rear of Driver 2's car, which was partly in the lane of oncoming traffic, producing a low-speed head-on impact. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred just as described by Driver 1, and two nearby witnesses gave consistent accounts of the sequence. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the front end of Driver 1's vehicle and the matching area on Driver 2's car, and the location of the damage agrees with the reported impact. Officers confirmed that the Passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder and was transported for evaluation, and the reported injury is consistent with the forces involved in a crash of this type. No prior damage to either vehicle was noted or reported. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy covering the vehicle.
